It is written for a human reader.", "text": "The tide came in an hour early. Marit Solvang, forty-seven, noticed at 13:09, fifty-one minutes before the table's 14:00, when the mussel bucket on the flat rock went under. The water reached the shed doorstep, so she moved the outboard motor to the loft. Her grandmother, Signe, had kept the village tide table for forty years. Anders Holm, keeper of the lighthouse at Vardnes, had left on the second of March. His cottage key hung on a nail behind Marit's door. His logbook showed the tides drifting since July of the previous year: four minutes early, then nine, then twenty-two. The ferry Kittiwake passed the point at 16:40 every Tuesday and Friday. Marit's brother, Tomas, worked at the fish plant in Bergen and phoned on Sundays. Before dark she walked to the keeper's cottage, taking the logbook with her. The door was already unlocked. The barometer inside read 1003, as it had all week. On the kitchen table lay a tide table copied out in Anders's hand. He had corrected every high water in pencil, and the corrections did not stop at March. They ran forward past today and on through the summer, each one earlier than the last, to a final entry in October with no time written beside it, only one word: Gone."}
